title: Dialogue Horizon Smoother: microwindow scheduler for mixed-length interactivity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Tune the continuous batching scheduler to improve latency and cost for mixed prompt/response workloads by introducing a dialogue-horizon smoothing layer (microwindow scheduler) that reduces KV cache fragmentation, evens GPU slab utilization, and enforces priority-fairness across interactive short-turn and long-turn requests.
problem_statement: Current continuous-batcher experiences latency spikes and KV cache churn when interactive workloads mix very short prompts (single-turn queries) and long responses (document generation). This leads to: 1) high eviction churn and KV fragmentation causing cold starts for hot dialogs, 2) inefficient GPU slab packing and memory tail waste, 3) unfair latency regressions where short-turn requests are delayed behind long responses despite tight SLOs.
proposal: Implement a microwindow 'horizon-smoother' layer on top of the existing continuous scheduler that: 1) groups requests into adaptive micro-windows (2-10ms) based on observed inter-arrival and length distribution, 2) assigns per-microwindow priorities with a fairness token to favor short-turn SLOs while allowing efficient coalescing with long-turn sequences, 3) maintains a KV-residency hint map to reduce cross-slab evictions by favoring colocated slots for follow-up turns, and 4) triggers lightweight epochal compaction to defragment GPU slabs when fragmentation exceeds a threshold. The component should expose tunables for latency budges, microwindow size, and KV-residency hysteresis.
acceptance_criteria: P90 tail latency for short-turn requests (<= 32 tokens) improves by >= 20% under mixed workload compared to baseline batching policy
Token-level GPU memory overhead reduces by >= 10% in sustained mixed load due to fewer KV evictions and improved slab packing
No user-visible increase in variance for long-response throughput (<= 5% throughput loss) under identical load
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-cluster
Unit + integration tests covering microwindow creation, priority token allocation, and KV-residency hint correctness
Dashboard panels show microwindow hit rate, KV hint hit/miss, slab fragmentation metric, and rollbackable alert thresholds

implementation_tasks: Task 1: Add microwindow queue and timer wheel to continuous-batcher core (ENG) — implement adaptive sizing and backlog drain policy
Task 2: KV-residency hint map service — small in-memory LRU per-GPU with estimated residency score and hysteresis
Task 3: Priority-fair token allocator — allow short-turn tokens to preempt coalescing when latency budget tight
Task 4: Epochal slab compactor — non-blocking lightweight compaction triggered off-peak or when fragmentation > threshold
Task 5: Instrumentation and metrics — microwindow_count, microwindow_duration_ms, kv_hint_hit_rate, slab_fragmentation_score, short_turn_p90
Task 6: Tests and replay harness — add replay scenarios for extreme mixlen skew and verify deterministic scheduler behavior
Task 7: Documentation and config knobs — Console flags, runtime-1.20 release notes, and operator playbook
rollout_plan: Feature will be behind a runtime flag. Start with single non-critical cluster in eu-west, monitor microwindow hit rate and short-turn P90 for 24h. If stable, expand to 3 clusters (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) over 72h. If short-turn P90 regresses > 10% or slab fragmentation increases > 15% rollback immediately. Final full rollout once stable over 7d.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive coalescing could increase latency for short-turns — Mitigation: conservative default microwindow size (3ms) and toggle to prefer fairness tokens
Risk: KV-residency map may add memory overhead — Mitigation: capped LRU with eviction policy and compressed residency score (8-bit) per entry
Risk: Epochal compaction may contend with inference — Mitigation: run compaction at low-priority background threads and throttle based on GPU idle fraction
Risk: Complexity increases operational burden — Mitigation: provide single runtime flag and default safe config; include automated rollback playbook
